BinFill.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    placed
        Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, oldest first. Start with an empty list when the memory is empty. Copy the carried-in list unchanged, except: if the execution steps shown at this step contain a frame with a cube 'held in the gripper' and the scene at this decision step shows the gripper open (about 100%) with no cube held, then the robot has just released a cube into the bin, so append that held cube's color once. Do not append when the step ends with a cube still held (that was a pick-up), when there are no execution steps (first step), or when the robot only pressed the button. Ignore cubes that appear or vanish on the table; only the held-then-released event counts. e.g. ["green", "green"]

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    The goal instruction names how many cubes of which color(s) must go into the bin before the button is pressed (e.g. 'two blue cubes' or 'one red cube and three green cubes'). Apply these rules at every decision step, using the scene shown and the memory field `placed` as updated at this step. Rule 1 (holding): If the scene at this decision step shows a cube 'held in the gripper', choose B: put it into the bin. This holds whatever `placed` contains. Rule 2 (done): If no cube is held and, for every color named in the goal, the number of entries of that color in `placed` is at least the number the goal asks for, choose C: press the button. The episode ends there. Rule 3 (pick): If no cube is held and some goal color still has fewer entries in `placed` than required, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at a cube of a color that is still needed. Where two colors are still needed, take the one with the larger remaining count (ties: either). Point at that cube's center as shown in the scene at this decision step. Prefer a cube of that color that was already visible at the same place in the earlier execution steps of this decision step (or, at step #1, simply any cube of that color), and avoid detections that flicker in and out or that lie on top of the bin's position; cubes of other colors are distractors and are never picked. Never point at the bin or the button. An episode starts in A at step #1: the gripper is raised out of the frame, `placed` is empty, so pick up a cube of a needed color. If a situation matches none of the rules (for example the fingers are closed but no cube is reported held, or no cube of a needed color is visible): if the fingers are partly closed treat it as holding and choose B; otherwise choose A pointing at the cube of a needed color nearest the gripper, and if none is visible at all, choose A pointing at any visible cube. Never choose C unless Rule 2 is satisfied.

ButtonUnmask.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    blue_cube_pos
        If this step shows a loose blue cube and no containers (the scene before the button is pressed), write the blue cube's [y, x] as shown. Otherwise copy the carried-in value unchanged; never overwrite it from a cube briefly exposed under a lifted container. e.g. [128, 141]
    green_cube_pos
        If this step shows a loose green cube and no containers (the scene before the button is pressed), write the green cube's [y, x] as shown. Otherwise copy the carried-in value unchanged. e.g. [88, 106]
    red_cube_pos
        If this step shows a loose red cube and no containers (the scene before the button is pressed), write the red cube's [y, x] as shown. Otherwise copy the carried-in value unchanged. e.g. [130, 79]
    picks_done
        Number of container pick-ups completed. Start at 0. If any execution step shown at this decision step says a container is held in the gripper, write carried-in value + 1; otherwise copy the carried-in value. e.g. 1

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    An episode starts in A (press the button): the first step shows the three loose cubes and no containers. Rule 1: if the step shows loose cubes and no containers anywhere and nothing held, choose A (press the button); at the same time record each cube's position in the memory fields. Rule 2: if the step shows containers on the table and the gripper is NOT holding a container, choose B (pick up the container). The target is the cube named in the goal at position picks_done+1 in the goal's order (first named cube when picks_done is 0, second named cube when picks_done is 1). Look up that cube's recorded position (blue_cube_pos / green_cube_pos / red_cube_pos) and point at the center of the container nearest to that recorded position, writing the point as [y, x]. Ignore containers that cover no recorded cube. Rule 3: if the step shows a container held in the gripper, choose C (put down the container). After that, Rule 2 applies again with the next cube in the goal. If all cubes named in the goal have already been picked (picks_done equals the number of cubes named), choose C if holding, otherwise B at the container nearest the last named cube. Unforeseen situation: if a container is held, choose C; if containers are visible and nothing is held, choose B at the container nearest the recorded position of the next goal cube; if no containers are visible, choose A.

ButtonUnmaskSwap.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    buttons_pressed
        Carried-in count plus 1 if any execution frame shown at this step says a button 'is pressed down'; otherwise the carried-in count. Start at 0. e.g. 1
    green_container
        [y, x] of the container hiding the green cube. If a frame shows the green cube uncovered and no containers, write the cube's position. When containers appear, take the one standing on the carried-in green position. Then follow that container through the frames shown: match each container to the nearest container in the previous frame; during a button press two containers glide around each other and finish swapped, so after the press the green container sits where the other moving container started. Write its position in the last frame shown. If the green cube is exposed by lifting its container, write the exposed cube's position. Start with the cube position seen at the first step. e.g. [109, 126]
    red_container
        [y, x] of the container hiding the red cube, kept exactly as green_container: cube position when visible, then the container that covered it, followed frame to frame (two movers during a press swap places), written at the last frame shown. e.g. [82, 152]
    blue_container
        [y, x] of the container hiding the blue cube, kept exactly as green_container: cube position when visible, then the container that covered it, followed frame to frame (two movers during a press swap places), written at the last frame shown. e.g. [102, 79]
    picked_colors
        Carried-in list; append the color of the cube that appears beneath a container shown 'held in the gripper' among this step's frames, if that color is not already in the list. Start empty. e.g. ["green"]

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    Start every episode in A (press the first button). Apply the first matching rule, after updating memory for this step: 1. If buttons_pressed is 0: A. 2. If buttons_pressed is 1: B. 3. If the scene at this decision step shows a container 'held in the gripper': D (put down the container). 4. If buttons_pressed is 2, nothing is held, and picked_colors is empty: C, pointing at the memory position (<color>_container) of the FIRST cube color named in the goal instruction (the one after 'hiding the'). Use the remembered container position, not the cube's original spot. 5. If buttons_pressed is 2, nothing is held, picked_colors has one entry, and the goal names a second cube ('another container hiding the ...'): C, pointing at the memory position of that SECOND color. This is the container that has not been lifted yet; do not point at the one just put down. 6. If every cube named in the goal is already in picked_colors and nothing is held: the task is done; answer D. Fallback: if the needed color's memory position is unknown, point C at the container nearest that cube's last known position; if no rule fits at all, answer the next unfinished item in goal order (A, B, C, D).

InsertPeg.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    grasp_point
        At the first decision step (demonstration shown, memory empty): find the demonstration frame where the gripper is at its lowest height (about 0.01-0.03) and the fingers have just gone from 100% open to about 22% open; pick the peg head or peg tail entry whose coordinates are nearest the gripper in that frame; then write that same end's coordinates as they appear in the start-of-execution scene (pegs are at their demonstration t=0 positions). At every later step copy the carried value unchanged. e.g. [114, 212]
    grasp_end
        At the first decision step: head if the nearest entry to the gripper at the demonstration grasp frame (lowest height, fingers just closed to ~22%) is a peg head, tail if it is a peg tail. At every later step copy the carried value unchanged. e.g. tail
    insert_side
        At the first decision step: look at the last few demonstration frames, where the gripper is low (height about 0.04), fingers still closed, and gripper y close to the aperture box y. If the gripper x in those frames is SMALLER than the aperture box x, write right; if LARGER, write left. At every later step copy the carried value unchanged. e.g. right

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    An episode starts in subgoal A. Rules: 1. If the scene shows no peg held in the gripper (no 'is held in the gripper' entry, fingers 100% open, gripper raised out of frame) and the demonstration steps are shown with an empty memory: choose A, pick up the peg by grasping one end, and point at grasp_point, i.e. the coordinates of the peg end (head or tail, matching grasp_end) that the demonstration gripper closed on, as that end appears in the current scene. Write grasp_point, grasp_end and insert_side at this step. 2. If the scene shows a peg end 'is held in the gripper' (fingers about 22% open, gripper raised): the pick is done. If insert_side is right, choose B, insert the peg from the right side. If insert_side is left, choose C, insert the peg from the left side. 3. If the scene shows no peg held and the memory already holds grasp_point (the pick failed or dropped): choose A again and point at grasp_point, using the current position of the peg end of class grasp_end nearest that stored point. 4. Any situation not covered: if nothing is held, choose A pointing at grasp_point (or, if grasp_point is unknown, at the peg end nearest the box); if something is held, choose B when insert_side is right or unknown, and C when insert_side is left. Carry all memory fields forward unchanged.

MoveCube.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    method
        The way the demonstration moved the cube. At the first decision step, read it from the demonstration steps: `pick` if the cube is marked as held in the gripper while the gripper is well above the table (height above about 0.08) with fingers partly closed (about 40-60% open) and the cube is then released over the target; `hook` if the stick (peg) is marked as held in the gripper with fingers closed to about 20-25% and is dragged against the cube toward the target; `push` if the fingers close to about 0% at table height (height below about 0.04) and the cube slides to the target without ever being lifted or any stick being held. At every later step copy the value carried in unchanged; never write `unknown` after the first step. e.g. hook
    holding
        What the robot has in its fingers at this decision step. Write `none` at the first decision step (nothing has been executed yet). Write `cube` if the execution steps shown descend the gripper onto the cube, close the fingers to about 40-60%, and rise again with the fingers still partly closed. Write `peg` if the execution steps shown descend the gripper onto the stick, close the fingers to about 20-25%, and rise again with the fingers still closed. Write `none` if the fingers at this step are 100% open or closed to about 0%. If the execution steps show no grasp, copy the value carried in. e.g. peg

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    The menu options need no target point; if a point is demanded anyway, point at the object the option names (the cube for C, D, E; the stick for A; the target for B and E would be the cube's destination, but prefer the cube). An episode starts at the first decision step with empty memory; first fill `method` from the demonstration steps, then choose by it. Rules, applied in whatever situation the policy stands in: - If `method` is `push`: choose C (close gripper and push the cube to the target). This is the only subgoal for a push episode. - If `method` is `pick` and `holding` is `none`: choose D (pick up the cube). - If `method` is `pick` and `holding` is `cube` (the execution steps just showed the fingers close to about 40-60% on the cube and the gripper rise): choose E (place the cube onto the target). - If `method` is `hook` and `holding` is `none`: choose A (pick up the peg). - If `method` is `hook` and `holding` is `peg` (the execution steps just showed the fingers close to about 20-25% on the stick and the gripper rise): choose B (hook the cube to the target with the peg). If a situation has no rule: if `method` cannot be told, decide by what the scene shows - fingers partly closed with the cube raised means E, fingers closed to about 20-25% with the stick raised means B; otherwise if the demonstration showed the stick held choose A, if it showed the cube lifted choose D, and if neither choose C. Never choose E without the cube in hand and never choose B without the peg in hand.

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    target_containers
        Ordered list of container positions, one per cube named in the goal, in the order the goal names them. At the first decision step (memory empty, demonstration steps shown): for each cube color named in the goal, read that cube's position from the demonstration steps before the containers appear, then take the container whose position is within a few pixels of it after the containers appear, and write that container's position; the cubes are no longer listed once containers are shown. Copy the list unchanged at every later step. e.g. [[81, 95], [66, 143]]
    picks_done
        Count of target containers picked up so far. Write 0 at the first decision step. At any later step, take the carried-in value and add one if the execution steps since the previous decision step show the fingers going from fully open to partly closed (about 40-60% open) with the gripper then raised, i.e. a container was grasped and lifted; otherwise copy the carried-in value. e.g. 1

Point at the container listed at index picks_done in target_containers (the first entry when picks_done is 0, the second when picks_done is 1). Write the point as that container's position with y reduced by about 3 pixels (e.g. container [84, 156] gives point [81, 158]). If the container visible at this step has drifted slightly from the stored position, point at the visible container nearest the stored position. Rule for B (put down): choose B whenever the gripper is holding a container (fingers partly closed, around 40-60% open, gripper raised after a grasp) and picks_done is less than N, meaning another target still has to be picked up. After the put-down the next decision step will show fingers fully open; then apply rule A for the next target. When picks_done equals N and the robot is holding a container, the task is complete and no further decision is expected; if asked anyway, choose B. THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    target_containers
        Ordered list of container positions [y, x], one per cube named in the goal instruction, in the order the goal names them. Write it at the first decision step (memory empty, demonstration steps shown) by this procedure, then copy it unchanged at every later step. Procedure: (1) from the first demonstration frames note the position of each named cube; (2) at the first frame where containers are listed instead of cubes, the named cube's container is the one nearest that cube's position; (3) follow that container through the remaining demonstration frames: at each frame it is the listed container nearest to its position in the previous frame, and when two moving containers are nearly equally near, keep the one that continues the same arc (the container that moved toward larger y keeps the larger y, the one that moved toward smaller y keeps the smaller y); containers that never move keep their position; (4) its position in the last demonstration frame is the entry. e.g. [[81, 90], [87, 134]]
    put_down_count
        Number of containers picked up and then put down so far. Write 0 at the first decision step. Add one to the carried-in value when the execution steps of the current step show the fingers reopening from about 46% to about 100% after being lowered over a container (a put-down just completed); otherwise copy the carried-in value. e.g. 1

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    An episode starts in A (pick up the container), with the point on the first entry of target_containers computed from the demonstration at that same step. Rules at any decision step: (1) If the scene shows the gripper raised with fingers partly closed (about 46% open), it is holding a container: choose B (put down the container). (2) If the fingers are fully open (about 100%) and put_down_count is less than the number of entries in target_containers, choose A and point at the container whose current listed position is nearest to target_containers[put_down_count + 1] (1-based: the first entry when put_down_count is 0, the second when it is 1); write the point as that container's listed position. (3) If the fingers are fully open and put_down_count equals the number of entries, every named container has been handled; choose A and point at the last entry of target_containers again (harmless repeat). If a situation matches none of these rules (e.g. gripper state unclear), pick the rule whose gripper description is closest: partly closed fingers mean B, open fingers mean A on the next unhandled target.
